candidate.answerReason: Each external tangent segment has length \(\sqrt{6^2-2^2}=4\sqrt2\). The hexagon consists of two trapezoids, each with area \(12\sqrt2\), agreeing with choice B.

methods.label: Split the hexagon into two trapezoids
methods.explanation:
Joining the centers divides the hexagon into two trapezoids. The radii perpendicular to the tangents provide their parallel sides.

[Figure 1](figures/2006_AMC_12B_Q15_question_fig1.svg)

Because the circles are externally tangent, their center distance is \(OP=2+4=6\). The tangent-radius property gives \(OA\perp AD\) and \(PD\perp AD\), so \(OA\parallel PD\). Since \(AD\) is an external tangent, both centers lie on the same side of it.

Draw through \(O\) a line parallel to \(AD\), meeting \(\overline{DP}\) at \(H\). Quadrilateral \(OADH\) is a rectangle, so
\[
DH=OA=2,\qquad PH=PD-DH=4-2=2,
\]
and \(OH=AD\). Triangle \(OPH\) is right at \(H\), giving
\[
AD=OH=\sqrt{OP^2-PH^2}
=\sqrt{6^2-2^2}=4\sqrt2.
\]
The same construction for the other external tangent gives \(BC=4\sqrt2\).

Segment \(OP\) divides the hexagon into trapezoids \(OADP\) and \(OBCP\), whose interiors do not overlap. Each has parallel sides of lengths \(2\) and \(4\), separated by the perpendicular tangent segment of length \(4\sqrt2\). Their combined area is therefore
\[
2\left(\frac{2+4}{2}\cdot4\sqrt2\right)
=\boxed{24\sqrt2},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses tangent-radius perpendicularity, a rectangle construction, the Pythagorean theorem, and the elementary trapezoid area formula.
